name: Han dynasty
period: 206 BCE–220 CE; Western Han 206 BCE–9 CE, Eastern Han 25–220 CE
region: China; narrow by capital/region when strict
summary: Imperial-era foundation with strong tomb-art, lacquer, bronze, silk, ceramic and expanding trans-Eurasian exchange evidence.

wardrobe.text: layered wrapped robes with belted silhouettes; exact cut varies by date, region and rank

textiles_materials.text: earthenware with pigment or lead glaze

hairstyle_headwear.text: hair and headwear should be selected from dated visual/tomb evidence rather than generic “ancient Chinese” defaults

architecture.text: Chang’an / Luoyang palace and warded urban context for capital scenes

interior_furniture.text: low furnishings and modeled architectural/tomb objects as evidence families

food_drink_tableware.text: lacquer and ceramic vessels; regional and class variation matters

musical_instruments.text: court/tomb ensembles including bells, drums and string/wind instruments

weapons_tools.text: swords, crossbows and military equipment appropriate to Han contexts

writing_calligraphy.text: seal/clerical-script context; do not invent decorative pseudo-Chinese text

ritual_custom.text: funerary mingqi and tomb programs are major surviving evidence but should not be treated as ordinary daily-life photographs

lighting_technology.text: oil lamps / flame lighting in interiors

incompatible_or_anachronistic.text: Ming/Qing porcelain motifs presented as Han
modern wuxia costume treated as documentary Han

prompt_fragments.wardrobe: Use a restrained Han-period wrapped and belted silhouette tied to the selected role; avoid generic later-dynasty costume vocabulary.
prompt_fragments.environment: Anchor architecture/material culture to Western Han Chang’an or Eastern Han Luoyang only when the chosen date supports it.

sources.supports: period split, capitals, exchange, material-culture examples

scope_note: Foundation pack: use as a bounded starting point, not an encyclopedia.
strict_reconstruction_note: Strict mode should narrow Western vs Eastern Han, location, social role, and source family.
